statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases within the low band after December NQ futures reopened into a contained 57-point range, while Stress stays elevated on a global long-end yield rout and a 3% crude rally.
recommendation: Thursday's Nasdaq-100 cash session based at 30,204.16, about 0.87% below the prior close, recovered the entire decline to 30,529.35 and settled at 30,478.86, up 0.03%. December NQ futures have since reopened from the daily CME maintenance break at 30,726.00, down 0.13%, inside a 30,708.50-30,765.25 band. Retracements completed in both directions across a 325-point cash range and the evening reopen is contained, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the Tail score measures, so Tail is set at 18 in the low band. Stress stays at 56 because the macro backdrop is genuinely difficult: the 10-year Treasury yield reached about 5.22%, its highest since 2007, the 30-year reached roughly 5.44%, its highest since 2004, global bonds sold off alongside them, WTI settled near $94.35 and Brent near $106.39 after a session high above $108, and roughly two-thirds odds of an October rate increase are now discounted. Index internals were dispersed rather than aligned, which under the risk contract lowers directional conviction rather than raising Tail. The narrow danger window covers Friday's 12:30Z Durable Goods release, the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:00Z final Michigan readings. Tail remains below the block threshold.
headline: Nasdaq-100 recovers its full intraday decline to close flat at 30,478.86; Tail eases to 18 as futures reopen quietly against a 2007-high 10-year yield
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,478.86, up 8.56 points or 0.03%, against a 30,470.29 prior close, after trading a 30,204.16 to 30,529.35 range. That low is about 0.87% below the prior close and the entire decline was recovered within the session, with the settle in the upper half of a 325-point range worth roughly 1.07%. December NQ futures have since reopened from the daily CME equity-futures maintenance break and print 30,726.00, down 0.13% against a 30,766.75 prior close, inside a narrow 30,708.50 to 30,765.25 band worth under 0.2%. This is the first hour of the current window in which an evening price path is actually observable, and what it shows is contained two-way trade rather than extension. Both observations matter directly for the risk contract, which defines Tail as the probability that mean reversion fails long enough to produce a persistent one-way path, repeated extension after failed pullbacks, or a delayed second leg. A complete intraday retrace followed by a contained futures reopen is direct evidence against that structure, and it is the reason Tail is set at 18 rather than higher. VIX closed at 15.67, up 3.23%, but well off a 16.57 session high and only modestly above a 15.34 low, so the volatility impulse decayed into the close rather than extending.

The stress backdrop is nevertheless harder than the equity close suggests, and it is where the genuine risk sits. The long end of the Treasury curve continued a months-long selloff: the 10-year yield reached about 5.22%, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year reached roughly 5.44%, its highest since 2004, with Reuters reporting the 30-year climbing more than three basis points on the day. Quoted levels are dispersed across venues, with the 10-year seen near 5.20% to 5.22% intraday, while the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 23 September carried the 2-year at 4.85%, the 10-year at 5.11% and the 30-year at 5.40%. The move was not confined to the United States: the 10-year Japanese government bond yield rose to its highest since 1996 and Bund and Gilt yields set fresh multi-year highs, which makes this a global term-premium event rather than a single-market one. Rate expectations moved with it, and roughly 64% odds of a 25 basis point increase in October and more than 48% for December are now discounted, with Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson noting that some modest further tightening may be warranted. Thursday's data supported that repricing: initial jobless claims came in at 197,000 against a 201,000 forecast, August new home sales printed 0.684 million against 0.626 million expected, and the Kansas City Fed composite index reached 14 against a forecast of 5.

Energy is the second pressure source and it is genuinely two-sided. WTI settled near $94.35, up about 2.7%, and Brent near $106.39, up about 3.4%, after Brent reached roughly $108 intraday when Iran-aligned Houthi forces fired missiles at Saudi cities including the Red Sea export terminal at Yanbu. Prices then came off those highs on reports that US and Iranian negotiators are exploring a phased agreement under which Iran would permit transit through the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for Washington lifting its naval blockade and easing sanctions. The same report is what allowed equities to pare their opening losses. Gulf shipping remains constrained, with only ten commodity vessels transiting the strait on Wednesday against a ten-day average of seventeen. Because that negotiation is unresolved and can resolve in either direction, it informs Stress, Confidence and the placement of the danger window rather than the current Tail score.

Index internals were dispersed rather than aligned, which is the single clearest argument against a higher Tail reading. Meta gained about 4.5% and Alphabet 1.34%, while Arm fell 7.88%, Qualcomm 1.51% and Broadcom 1.3%; Intel rose 3.91% and AMD 2.38% against declines in Nvidia and Micron's peers, leaving semiconductor dispersion near 3.5 percentage points with three advancers against four decliners. At sector level, Communication Services gained 1.67% while Technology fell 0.37% and Consumer Cyclical fell 0.45%. Oracle fell after issuing a force majeure notice on a New Mexico data-centre project, and MGM Resorts dropped about 10% after a withdrawn takeover bid, but neither is index-defining. Under the risk contract, conflicting internals reduce directional conviction and support the mixed dominant mode; they do not mechanically raise Tail. A hawkish repricing, a record-territory yield move, an energy shock and high-importance headlines all raise Stress and inform Confidence. Tail would additionally require observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow or failed retracements, or a hold near session extremes, none of which occurred in the cash session or in the futures reopen.

The forecast keeps conditional Tail inside the low-to-watch band for all 24 slots and never reaches a blocking level, because a blocking level would assert structure that is not observed at the assessment cutoff. It stays at 18 to 19 through the thin late-evening and mid-Asian hours, enters the watch band at the Tokyo open where global long-end repricing is first tested live, builds to 22 or 23 across the European morning where the published lookback last saw Tail reach its only orange print, and peaks at 24 across the 12:30Z Durable Goods release, the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:00Z final Michigan sentiment and inflation-expectation readings. A secondary conditional rise to 23 covers the Friday power hour, when quarter-end index rebalancing and week-end squaring concentrate flow. The final slot falls to 16 because CME equity futures close for the week at 21:00Z and do not reopen until Sunday evening, so no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path can exist inside it.

Confidence is set at 87. Current levels for the cash index, December futures, VIX, the Treasury curve and both crude benchmarks were taken from primary quote and release pages during this run, the seven-day US calendar was read from a scheduled-event feed, and every news item cited in the hourly forecast was retrieved and read rather than inferred. Two evidence gaps hold Confidence below the very-high band. First, intraday yield quotes are dispersed across venues, so exact prints are reported as ranges. Second, the shared Finviz context was about 103 minutes old at the cutoff, beyond its 90-minute freshness limit, and partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable; it was therefore used only as stale latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor tone and for headline discovery, and never as evidence of current Nasdaq-100 structure.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 published hours held a watch-band regime with a single orange print. Tail ran 20 through Wednesday's late evening, eased to 17-19 across the Asian overnight, then rebuilt through a trend-down European morning to a 25 peak at 09:00Z, the only BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES slot in the window. Across Thursday's US session Tail oscillated between 19 and 24 without establishing persistent one-way structure, and the last four published hours settled at 21, 20, 19 and 19 as the cash session completed its retrace. Stress climbed from 51-52 overnight to 56-57 by the close as long-end yields and crude both extended. Confidence held in the 85-88 band throughout.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from an already-observed quiet futures reopen through the Asian and European sessions into Friday's US cash session and the futures weekly close. Conditional Tail stays in the low-to-watch band and never reaches a blocking level, because raising it further would assert structure that does not exist at the assessment cutoff. It holds at 18-19 through the thin late-evening and mid-Asian hours, enters the watch band at the Tokyo open where the global long-end move is first tested live, builds to 22-23 through the European morning where the lookback's only orange print occurred, and peaks at 24 across the 12:30Z Durable Goods release, the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:00Z final Michigan readings. Stress peaks at 62 in the cash-open hour and stays elevated all session on record-territory long-end yields, October hike pricing and an unresolved Gulf negotiation. A secondary rise to 23 covers the Friday power hour into quarter-end. The final slot falls to 16 because the futures week closes at 21:00Z with no tradable price path until the Sunday reopen.
